solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A right angry tirade, out-and-out

parts.note: a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: Someone launches into a furious, thoroughgoing rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrant is an intensifying adjective meaning utter or complete, as in an arrant fool.

clue.text: Get better engineers on top of roof?

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a roof's outer covering may be called its cover

explanation.surface: Will the engineers mend the roof covering?
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain health, which is to get better.

clue.text: One for ventilating anger in middle of Carmarthen

indicators.note: in puts the word for anger within the central pair of letters
middle of means only the central letters of the town name are used

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone in a Welsh town vents their rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Carmarthen is a town in south-west Wales; 'One for ventilating' sounds like a fan, but means a clothes-drying frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a frame for drying or airing clothes, a thing used for ventilating them.

clue.text: Defiant leader of union advanced after brief upset

indicators.note: after means the reversed brief word comes first and the union letter and advanced follow it
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: curt means brief or abrupt

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of the word

parts.note: lent means advanced, as money is advanced on loan

explanation.surface: A union boss pushed on defiantly after a quick setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a trimming signal but gives CURT, which 'upset' turns to TRUC.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculent means eager to fight or argue, aggressively defiant.

clue.text: A roguish one about to become lawless

parts.note: the indefinite article a can be written as an
arch means mischievous or roguish, as in an arch smile
I is the Roman numeral for one
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A mischievous character is on the verge of turning into an outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' gives AN, its other form before a vowel; 'to become' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic describes a state without order or government, which is a lawless state.

clue.text: Walkers heading off may be country folk

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: marchers are walkers

explanation.surface: Hikers setting off may be rural people.
explanation.walkthrough: THE ARCHERS is a long-running BBC radio soap about a farming village, so its family are country folk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archers are the farming family of the BBC radio serial set in rural England.

clue.text: Outside it's barren, inside it's cold, bitter

indicators.note: inside places the letter for cold within the word for barren

parts.note: arid means dry and barren
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A grim landscape: desolate outdoors and chilly indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' marks ARID as the outer piece and 'inside' marks C as the inner one.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp and bitter in taste or smell.

clue.text: Money I had to pocket before being given the push

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: to pocket means to take in, so the letters for I had enclose the old word for before

parts.note: I'd is short for I had
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Someone pockets cash before being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cashiered is to be dismissed from service, especially the armed forces, so given the push.

clue.text: One little lady in charge of keeping the books is brainless

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the lady and charge letters hold the books

parts.note: Di is a short form of the name Diana
OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A diminutive woman responsible for the accounts is dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the books' are not accounts but the Old Testament, OT; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means very stupid, as if lacking a brain.

clue.text: Oxford college's rustic porch is vandalised

indicators.note: something vandalised is wrecked and broken up, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has damaged the countrified porch of an Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' rearranges the thirteen letters of RUSTIC PORCH IS; the 's after college is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpus Christi is one of the colleges of Oxford University, founded in 1517.

clue.text: Disallow sin in botanical body

indicators.note: in places the word for sinning within the plant part

parts.note: an ovule is the part of a plant's ovary that becomes a seed
to err is to sin or go astray

explanation.surface: Someone forbids wrongdoing within a society of botanists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botanical body' suggests a learned society of botanists, but it is a part of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrule a decision or objection is to reject it with superior authority, disallowing it.

clue.text: Delicate period needing brief international intervention

indicators.note: intervention means one piece comes between the letters of the other

parts.note: a day is a period of time
INT is the short form of international

explanation.surface: A tricky time that requires some quick help from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainty means small, fine and delicate in appearance or manner.

clue.text: Woman at match admits 'Good game!'

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the woman encloses the letter for good

parts.note: a match here is a marriage, and the woman at it is the bride

explanation.surface: A female spectator at a sporting fixture concedes it was a fine contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests sport, but it is a wedding match, giving BRIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players in two partnerships.

clue.text: Pumped for information, being exposed down below maybe?!

definitions.meaning: questioned closely after a mission to learn what happened
read playfully, having had one's underpants taken off

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as DE-BRIEFED, with briefs, a British word for underpants, removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be debriefed is to be questioned about a completed task, i.e. pumped for information.

clue.text: Bag a group of people for event on sports day

parts.note: a sack is a large bag
a race is a group of people sharing descent

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to grab a team for a school sports contest.
explanation.walkthrough: A sports day is the annual athletics event at a British school, with novelty races.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack race is a novelty race where children hop along with their legs inside sacks.

clue.text: Girl sitting on rug in church is someone you're at school with

indicators.note: in places the girl and rug within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: in a down clue the girl sits on top of the rug

parts.note: a lass is a girl
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A girl perched on a mat in church is a schoolfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A classmate is a fellow pupil in the same class at school.

clue.text: More than one accolade attempts to stifle objection

indicators.note: to stifle means to smother, so the attempts wrap round the objection

parts.note: tries are attempts
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Several honours are efforts to silence a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Tributes are acts or statements of praise, plural accolades.

clue.text: What's left I'd reuse in a different way

indicators.note: in a different way tells you to put the letters into another order

explanation.surface: Leftovers that someone plans to recycle differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is the remainder left after something is removed or used.

clue.text: Chess player to disappear into the blue

indicators.note: into puts the vanishing word within the word for the blue

parts.note: the blue is a poetic phrase for the sky
to pass, as in pass away or pass out of sight, is to disappear

explanation.surface: A chess player vanishes into thin air.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Spassky was the Soviet world chess champion who lost to Bobby Fischer in 1972.
explanation.definitionFit: Spassky was a world chess champion, so an example of a chess player.

clue.text: Enthusiasm in a party given by ancient city entertaining king

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the king is held inside the other letters

parts.note: a do is a party
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Excitement at a celebration put on by an old city where a monarch is a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour means passion or fervent enthusiasm for something.

clue.text: Weird upper-class grandma enthralling children at the outset

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the grandma word holds the letter

parts.note: nanny is an informal word for grandmother

indicators.note: at the outset takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An odd posh granny charms the kids right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grandma' points to NAN, but NANNY is needed, with C after its first N.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny means strange and unsettling, which is weird.

clue.text: Spots food in military refectory (no starter provided)

indicators.note: in places the food within the canteen word
no starter means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a mess is where members of the armed forces eat
pies are food

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the army canteen serves only main courses, no first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no starter' removes M from MESS, leaving ESS, which holds PIES; 'starter' plays on the meal course.
explanation.definitionFit: Espies means catches sight of, which is what spots means as a verb.

clue.text: Characters from Lahore rose up, feeling more aggrieved

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top
characters from means a run of letters is taken from the words

explanation.surface: People in Lahore rose up in growing resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters from' takes RE ROS from 'Lahore rose', and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorer is the comparative of sore in the sense of upset or resentful, so more aggrieved.

clue.text: Take away a bishop's religious pamphlet

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, and the possessive supplies an S
a tract is a short religious pamphlet

explanation.surface: Grab a churchman's booklet.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract something is to remove or take it away, often by stealth.

clue.text: Beast in river almost squashing duck

indicators.note: in a down clue the river sits on top of the duck, squashing it
almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the Rhine is a major European river
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: An animal in a river almost flattens a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhino, short for rhinoceros, is a large horned beast.

clue.text: A root infested badly? It leads to many a tree being destroyed

definitions.text: It leads to many a tree being destroyed

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A tree root is badly diseased, a reminder of how forests get cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the thirteen letters of A ROOT INFESTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Deforestation is the clearing of forests, which means felling large numbers of trees.

clue.text: With kindness, offer to meet learner before end of day

parts.note: to tender is to offer
L is the learner driver's plate

indicators.note: end of means take only the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A suitor kindly proposes to meet a student late in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderly means gently and with affection, which is acting with kindness.

clue.text: Emma is one English maiden stabling horse

indicators.note: stabling means housing an animal, so the horse is held between the letters

parts.note: M stands for maiden, a cricket over with no runs
a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: Emma is an English girl who keeps a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma is the Jane Austen novel named after its heroine, so it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is a title or name taken from a person, as the novel Emma takes its heroine's name.
